theory.intro: A **similarity statement** names two similar figures with their vertices in **matching order**, joined by the symbol $\sim$, e.g. $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle LMK$. The order does the work: it records which vertices correspond, so corresponding angles and corresponding sides can be read straight off the letters.
facts: $\sim$ means "is similar to": $ABCD \sim EFGH$ says the two quadrilaterals are similar.
Vertices are listed in matching order: in $ABCD \sim EFGH$, $\angle ABC = \angle EFG$ and side $AB$ corresponds to side $EF$.
Corresponding vertices are found by matching equal angles, not by matching positions on the page — a rotated or reflected figure changes nothing.
A statement with the letters out of matching order is wrong even when the figures really are similar.
steps: Identify the corresponding vertices by matching equal angles.
Write the vertices of both figures in matching order.

foundation.solution_text:
$\angle A=\angle L=70^{\circ}$
$\angle B=\angle M=60^{\circ}$
$\angle C=\angle K=50^{\circ}$
$\therefore \triangle ABC \sim \triangle LMK$

Matching the equal angles around each figure: $A\leftrightarrow L$, $B\leftrightarrow M$, $C\leftrightarrow N$, $D\leftrightarrow P$, $E\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\therefore ABCDE \sim LMNPQ$

foundation.question_text: The pentagons $GHJKL \sim PQRST$ are similar. Which side of the second pentagon corresponds to side $JK$?
foundation.solution_text:
$J$ is the third letter and $K$ is the fourth, so they match $R$ and $S$.
Side $JK$ corresponds to side $RS$.

foundation.question_text: Given $\triangle DEF \sim \triangle STU$, which angle of $\triangle STU$ corresponds to $\angle EFD$?
foundation.solution_text:
Matching the letters: $D\leftrightarrow S$, $E\leftrightarrow T$, $F\leftrightarrow U$.
$\angle EFD$ corresponds to $\angle TUS$.

The single arcs show $\angle P=\angle X$ and the double arcs show $\angle Q=\angle Y$, so the remaining angles give $\angle R=\angle Z$.
A reflection does not change the shape, so the vertices still match by equal angles.
$\therefore \triangle PQR \sim \triangle XYZ$

foundation.question_text: The quadrilaterals $PQRS \sim WXYZ$ are similar. Which angle of the second quadrilateral corresponds to $\angle QRS$?
foundation.solution_text:
Matching the letters: $Q\leftrightarrow X$, $R\leftrightarrow Y$, $S\leftrightarrow Z$.
$\angle QRS$ corresponds to $\angle XYZ$.

foundation.question_text: Given $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle FGH$, list the three pairs of corresponding sides.
foundation.solution_text:
$AB$ corresponds to $FG$
$BC$ corresponds to $GH$
$CA$ corresponds to $HF$

development.solution_text:
$\angle A$ is shared by both triangles.
$\angle ADE=\angle ABC$, corresponding angles on parallel lines
$\angle AED=\angle ACB$, corresponding angles on parallel lines
$\therefore \triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$

$\angle KAL=\angle MAN$, vertically opposite angles
$\angle AKL=\angle AMN$, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\angle ALK=\angle ANM$, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\therefore \triangle KAL \sim \triangle MAN$

The vertices must be listed in matching order, found by matching equal angles — $\angle A$ is a right angle but $\angle P$ is not, so $P$ cannot correspond to $A$.
Matching the right angles and following the boundary: $A\leftrightarrow R$, $B\leftrightarrow S$, $C\leftrightarrow P$, $D\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\therefore ABCD \sim RSPQ$

The apex angles correspond, so $M\leftrightarrow P$; following the boundary from there matches $N\leftrightarrow Q$, $J\leftrightarrow R$, $K\leftrightarrow S$, $L\leftrightarrow T$.
$\therefore JKLMN \sim RSTPQ$

The long arm of the first L runs $A$ to $B$, and the matching long arm of the second runs $R$ to $S$, so $A\leftrightarrow R$ and $B\leftrightarrow S$; following the boundary matches $C\leftrightarrow T$, $D\leftrightarrow U$, $E\leftrightarrow P$, $F\leftrightarrow Q$.
$\therefore ABCDEF \sim RSTUPQ$

development.question_text: The pentagons $ABCDE$ and $VWXYZ$ are similar, with $\angle A=\angle V$, $\angle B=\angle W$, $\angle C=\angle X$, $\angle D=\angle Y$ and $\angle E=\angle Z$. Kai writes $ABCDE \sim ZYXWV$. Explain his error and write a correct similarity statement.
development.solution_text:
Kai listed the second pentagon's letters in reverse: his statement pairs $\angle A$ with $\angle Z$, but $\angle A=\angle V$.
The vertices must be written in matching order.
$\therefore ABCDE \sim VWXYZ$

practice.masteryOmitted: Vertex-order naming is a single-step convention; the hardest honest in-skill cases (overlapping, reflected and rotated figures) already sit in development, and any further twist crosses into similarity testing or unknown-side work owned by sibling skills.
